summary: Part 7 covers units s0077–s0078 and s0220–s0255 of Jinshu 109: Murong Huang's maternal-kin memorial after hearing 庾亮薨, plus the letter to Yu Bing. Yu Liang's death (AD 340), Bing/Yi succession (AD 340), Emperor Cheng as memorial addressee (AD 340), the Su Jun–Zu Yue rising (AD 327–328), and Empress Dowager Yu's death (AD 328) are supported from the Chinese with Chengdi-annals conversions. The Zhou–Han exempla (Shen Bo through Zhang Yu) are defective in the same way as part 5's Cao Cao/Sima Zhao rows: they are only cited in the AD 340 memorial, yet carry imported life spans and active hints. Separately, hints-p083 merges 327–328 and 340 into one career window, and claim-573/hints-p097 assign Emperor Cheng a reign-wide 325–342 span for undated 陛下. No birth or age is stated in the owned units; the only deaths are Yu Liang and the Empress Dowager. This is not a full-chapter approval.

itemChecks.event: Yu Liang's own death, which Murong Huang learns of before submitting the maternal-kin memorial.
itemChecks.reason: s0077 explicitly records 又聞庾亮薨 as the narrative trigger. Jinshu Chengdi annals date that death to 咸康六年正月庚子 = AD 340 (reign-year label; no month asserted from this chapter alone).

itemChecks.event: Yu Liang's own prior exercise of maternal-uncle power that the memorial blames for driving Su Jun and Zu Yue to ruin the state.
itemChecks.reason: s0232 names 故司空亮 as cause of 蘇峻、祖約…敗國. That rebellion is the Xianhe 2–3 event (AD 327–328) in Chengdi's annals; the memorial may attest the earlier life event. Window 327–328 is uncertainty about that rebellion episode, not a dynasty-long career span.
